messages:
jamie: FYI DAST on staging flagged a potential open-redirect on /auth/callback when the redirect param is present. I ran it twice, looks reproducible but only when the scan doesn't log in first.
mira: can you paste the HTTP trace? maybe it's the test harness following 302s differently. :thinking:
jamie: snippet from the DAST run:
```
GET /auth/callback?next=https://evil.example.com 302 -> Location: /login
GET /login 200
GET /auth/callback?next=https://evil.example.com 200 (rendered page with next param echoed)  
```
mira: OK that looks like the app echoes `next` into a hidden input, not performing host-checking. That could be an open redirect if later code redirects to that value. Is there a follow redirect that sends users to external host? 
jamie: not in our normal flow -- but DAST followed the payload into a JS redirect path that only happens after a simulated login step. I think the scanner's unauthenticated flow is tricking it into a dev-only debug path. scanner-bot: DAST job #4456 completed. Findings: potential "open redirect", confidence: medium, evidence: included. Link: https://ci.redwood/dast/4456
leo: assign to web-auth team + security review. @priya can you confirm whether the post-login redirect performs host allowlist checks?
priya: taking a look. Quick note: our login shim sets `window.location = next || '/'` in one branch for legacy clients. That's a bug but only used by our old mobile shim (feature flag off for prod). 
priya: repro steps I used: emulate legacy mobile UA, hit /auth/callback with external next, then login flows set location to next. 
mira: thanks. So two things: 1) fix legacy shim to validate hosts, 2) mark this DAST finding as a true positive and ticket it. We should also document the evidence (screenshots + request/response) in the ticket for audit. 
jamie: will open SEC-789 with evidence. Suggest adding a temporary SCA (scan change approval) — we need a waiver window for the mobile shim while we roll the fix to Dedicated customers.
leo: for waivers: we need an approval audit trail. Current security-review only records GH approval comments. Can we add an audit-log entry when sec approves the waiver (so infra can query who allowed it and for how long)? 
mira: +1. We should add a small webhook from the security-review app to push approval events into our audit log (append-only). Proposal: when reviewer posts `/sec-approve waiver:SEC-789 expires:2026-05-10 reason:legacy-mobile-shim` the review bot emits an audit event to the keystore-backed audit-store. 
jamie: required fields: approver, ticket, expiry, scope, evidence link. Keep TTL so infra auto-expunges ephemeral grants.
leo: implementation notes: audit-store expects an HMAC-signed payload. The review bot needs KMS access to sign tokens. We'll need a minimal RBAC grant for `service-account:sec-review-bot` to call `kms.sign` only. That keeps the key usage scoped.
priya: we might already have a short-lived service account used by scanners. But be careful: do not give decrypt rights. Only sign. Also add a rotation policy and an alert if signing requests spike.
mira: agree. Also add CI gating: block merge until SEC-789 has either a fix PR or an approved waiver recorded in audit-store. That prevents silent bypasses.
jamie: timeline: I'll open the ticket + attach DAST evidence, add repro steps and mark P2. ETA: PR for shim fix by EOD tomorrow. I'll stub the `/sec-approve` hook in review-bot this week (no KMS call until we get a scoped grant request). 
leo: I'll start the RBAC request template for IAM: minimal `kms.sign` for `sec-review-bot`; include justification and expiry. CC: infra oncall.
scanner-bot: note: DAST false-positive rate for unauthenticated flows is ~18% historically — consider enabling authenticated scans for staging to reduce noise. 
mira: yep let's flip authenticated scans for staging after we have a test service account that mirrors production flows. Add that to the ticket as mitigation.
jamie: thanks team. I'll post SEC-789 link when created. :thumbsup:
